description.narrative: Feed the Future India Triangular Training Program: USAID partners with the Indian Ministry of Agricultures premier institute the National Institute of Agricultural Extension Management (MANAGE) to train 1,500 agricultural practitioners from 11 African and 6 Asian countries on specialized farming practices to improve productivity and income. Phase I of the program trained 219 participants from Kenya, Liberia, and Malawi in agricultural marketing, dairy management, food processing and other best practices to prevent post-harvest losses. These farmers, food processors, extension workers, and policymakers are now implementing new farming practices that improve food and nutritional security in their countries and regions. Following the successes of these three countries, Phase II, launched in 2016, expanded to include training for hundreds of additional professionals, helping increase the agricultural stability of 17 target countries. A total of 44 training programs including 32 based in India and 12 based in the target countries will be completed by March 2020. As of September 2017, ten programs were implemented involving 289 trainees.

title.narrative: HIV/AIDS - Host Country Strategic Information Capacity (HIV)

description.narrative: HIV/AIDS - Basic health care and support, which includes: all clinic-based and home/community-based activities for HIV-infected adults, children, and their families that are aimed at optimizing the quality of life for HIV-infected clients and their families throughout the continuum of illness by the means of symptom diagnosis and relief, psychological and spiritual support, clinical monitoring, related laboratory services and management of opportunistic infections (excluding TB) and other HIV/AIDS-related complications (including pharmaceuticals), and culturally-appropriate end-of-life care. Basic health care and support also includes clinic-based and home/community-based support, social and material support such as nutrition support, legal aid, and housing, and training and support of caregivers. Clinic-based and home/community-based care and support activities for HIV-positive children within programs for orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS would fall under sub-element 1.1.8 (Orphans and Vulnerable Children). ARV treatment should be coded under sub-element 1.1.10 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Drugs) and sub-element 1.1.11 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Services).

title.narrative: HIV/AIDS - Host Country Strategic Information Capacity (HIV)

description.narrative: HIV/AIDS - Improve the lives of orphans and other vulnerable children and families affected by HIV/AIDS. Strengthen communities to meet the needs of orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, supporting community-based responses, helping children and adolescents to meet their own needs, creating a supportive social and policy environment. Activities could include training caregivers, increasing access to education, economic support, targeted food and nutrition support, and legal aid. Institutional responses would also be included. ARV treatment of children is excluded from this category and should be coded under Sub-Element 1.1.10 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Drugs) and Sub-Element 1.1.11 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Services). title.narrative: Adding Precision Supervision to CommCare and Evaluating it at Scale

description.narrative: India deploys over two million frontline health workers throughout the country to provide maternal and child health services through home visits, antenatal care, and nutrition programs. Despite these and other significant efforts, India has more neonatal mortalities than any other country and an estimated 44,000 women die each year due to preventable pregnancy-related causes. One way to improve outcomes is by arming frontline workers with digital tools that improve the efficacy of their work. Dimagi's open source CommCare platform has been used to equip over 750,000 frontline workers with mobile apps in over 80 countries. Strong evidence, including several randomized controlled trials, demonstrates that equipping frontline workers with CommCare improves client outcomes such as maternal mortality, low birth weight, and malnutrition in the first 1,000 days after birth. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, Dimagi will build and test predictive analytics using the vast amounts of government-owned data captured by its platform and leverage recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) to predict future events. Dimagi will apply predictive analytics to help existing frontline workers and their supervisors proactively identify and prioritize high risk clients, increase diagnosis accuracy, detect outbreaks, and improve healthcare delivery to remote areas. At scale, the AI techniques developed through this project will run at pennies per person. Dimagi and its partners at IDInsight will design an evaluation and obtain necessary permissions to test these techniques at scale. Through the power of predictive analytics, this work has the potential to directly benefit 27 million people over the next five years, not only in health, but also agriculture, education, and other sectors around the world.

title.narrative: Every child counts! Scaling up a successful games based curriculum

description.narrative: Despite significant gains in primary school enrollment, 125 million children worldwide are not developing basic math and reading skills. Many children in India are not ready for primary school: 43 percent of first graders in rural areas cannot recognize letters and 36 percent cannot recognize single-digit numbers (ASER 2018). Evidence shows that achievement gaps between low and high-performing children widen steadily over time, and few children who start behind ever catch up. To help prepare young children for success in primary school, MIT's Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab at the Institute for Financial Management and Research in India (IFMR) (J-PAL South Asia) has applied decades of research on how children learn in order to develop a collection of simple, low-cost games that engage children's natural math capacity to improve their formal math skills. Proven effective by multiple randomized controlled trials, the Math Games program requires only 45-minute sessions, three times per week and can be effectively delivered by lightly-trained volunteers or government teachers. With support from Development Innovation Ventures (DIV), J-PAL South Asia is providing technical assistance and monitoring and evaluation support to expand the program in Tamil Nadu's public school system and partnering with state governments and the Indian NGO Pratham to expand Math Games to three more states (Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, and Punjab). In addition, DIV is supporting a long-term follow-up studyled by cognitive psychologist Elizabeth Spelke of Harvard University and Nobel Prize-winning economist Esther Duflo of MITthat measures the persistence of the program's impact on the children from the original study. As Math Games continues to scale, it has the potential to significantly improve the foundational skills of 2.8 million children across these four states.

title.narrative: A Tough Call: Impacts of Mobile Technology on Women's Employment

description.narrative: In developing countries, as many as 80 percent of women do not have access to the internet. India has one of the widest sex-based digital divides with a gap of 15 percent for mobile phone ownership and 33 percent for mobile internet use. Unequal access to information between men and women can cause underinvestment in children, poor use of health services, and limit the reach of state-sponsored social protection programs. To narrow the divide, the Government of Indias Sanchar Kranti Yojana (SKY) program provided millions of free smartphones and data plans to female heads of household in Chhattisgarhone of Indias poorest statesin 2018. The program paired distribution with messaging campaigns and guidance on how women could use mobile phones productively. Rigorous evidence on the effects of increasing womens access to technology is currently minimal. With support from Development Innovation Ventures, a research team led by Yale University will evaluate the impacts of SKY to learn how mobile phone distribution affected women in terms of phone use and engagement; banking activity and income generation; access to information and networks; decision making and mobility; mental health; and social norms around the acceptability of women using mobile phones and how it affected communities in terms of economic activities, wages, and migration. This evaluation will also investigate if and how the program changed peoples knowledge of current events and use of government services, whether they are more likely to use social media, and whether they are more likely to believe social media rumors and misinformation. This research will generate critical evidence on the efficacy of programs designed to close the sex-based digital divide, and inform future research and policy design, including that of several programs that are already in planning stages by various state-level governments in India.

title.narrative: Piloting a Business Model for Sensor-Controlled Riverbank Filtration

description.narrative: To make more high-quality water available for agriculture and ease the demand on groundwater resources, The Energy and Resources Institute (TERI) and the University of Rhode Island built upon a proven water treatment system that converts low-quality river water into high-quality irrigation water by pumping it from the river toward a riverbank well. There, auto-regenerative filtration processes remove dissolved and suspended contaminants, including bacteria, without chemicals or complex equipment. TERIs innovation adds field sensors that determine how much water is needed to irrigate crops and uses that information to pump only the amount of water needed, which prevents overuse.

title.narrative: Evaluating the Effects of a Well-being Curriculum on Student Success

description.narrative: An alarming one in four children and adolescents in India grapple with mental health disorders, which perpetuate educational inequities and entrench cycles of poverty. Yet evidence-based mental health interventions are scarce. Within Reach, through its partner Labhya, is working in public schools in partnership with three state governments in India to pioneer a social-emotional learning (SEL) program. In Tripura, this program is called Saharsh, which means joy in Bengali, integrates mindfulness practices and interactive storytelling sessions into daily 30-minute classes, aiming to equip primary school children with crucial coping skills and emotional resilience. Labhya is rigorously testing its curriculum with a large-scale randomized controlled trial (RCT) in the state of Tripura, where the government has expressed interest in using this evidence to adapt and scale student mental health programming. With support from Development Innovation Ventures (DIV), Labhya will collect follow-up data for the RCT and monitor processes to measure teachers adherence to the curriculum. This evaluation is supported by the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL), the Weiss Fund, and the Fund for Innovation in Development. The results will inform government support and scale-up efforts, possibly benefiting millions of children across India and beyond

title.narrative: Piloting a Machine Learning-Powered English Tutor

description.narrative: Research has shown that for elementary schoolchildren in India, developing literacy and fluency in English can have a large impact on university admissions, skill development, and lifetime earnings. India faces a growing shortage of qualified English teachers and tutors that disproportionately affects poor populations. The implementing partner (IP) developed a digital personalized adaptive learning platform for English literacy that uses machine learning and natural language processing to detect and diagnose speech errors made by elementary school students while reading aloud. The IP then delivers research-backed, customized reading instruction ranging from word recognition skills to reading comprehension. The platform builds on over 30 years of lab-based research and has reached over three million students in the U.S. and 17 additional countries. The IP will pilot and test their product with approximately 4,700 low-income primary school students throughout India. The team will investigate implementation challenges, student take-up, engagement, and retention with the aim to apply what they learn in adapting the platform for scale in Indias government and affordable school sectors. This approach has the potential to improve reading skills while also generating information on the use of machine learning to improve English literacy in low-income communities, contributing to an important body of knowledge.

title.narrative: Testing a Digital Tool for Healthcare Workers to Reduce Child Mortality

description.narrative: Terre des Hommes developed the Integrated e-Diagnostic Approach (IeDA), a digitalized IMCI job aid that hasbeen shown to improve healthcare worker performance and protocol adherence. The IeDA software is updated as best practices change, helping to standardize care and support evidence-based clinical decisions in real time. At the end of a patient consultation, IeDA gives healthcare providers an analysis of signs, symptoms, and test results, and suggests a diagnosis, which the provider can then use to propose treatment. Terre des Hommes has been using IeDAin the state of Jharkhand since 2020. With DIV support, Terre des Hommes will conduct a randomized controlled trial of IeDA in India to evaluate the impact of IeDA on the percentage of children under five who are correctly diagnosed and treated.

description.narrative: (India): .USAID/India will implement a new activity entitled Technical.Assistance to the Government of India (GOI) for the Swachh Bharat Mission that.is a follow-on to the previous identically named activity. This "phase.two" will fund national project management units supporting both the Swachh.Bharat (Clean India) and Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation.(AMRUT) GOI missions that are working to end open defecation in India. As.the Swachh Bharat Mission comes to a close in 2019, AMRUT will continue the.work to ensure open defecation free status is maintained and the treatment of.liquid wastes is improved in urban areas. USAID's assistance under this.activity will directly support the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.(MoHUA) and provide targeted support to two states and five cities. The.activity will scale successful WASH approaches to strengthen governance and.policy frameworks, program management, and institutional capacities at national.and sub-national levels to plan, budget and monitor WASH progress. The.activity will also build the capacity of municipal officials to accelerate the.implementation of key Swachh Bharat components by introducing them to the tools.and progress achieved by other cities, which have already made substantial.gains under the initiative.The activity will also facilitate public institution engagement with the.private sector in WASH value chains by identifying financing needs and options.and developing private sector engagement strategies for municipal governments. .The activity will also develop city-specific financing plans for five cities.(three in Uttar Pradesh and two in Rajasthan)... .

(India): Using FY2019 funds, USAID/India will continue its support for the Moving India towards Sanitation for All (MISAAL) activity which is implemented by the Urban Management Centre (UMC). Broadly speaking, the activity focuses on building the capacity of municipal officials to ensure improved access to WASH infrastructure development and the adoption of appropriate WASH related behaviours. More specifically, the MISAAL activity provides technical assistance to the municipal governments of the cities of Ahmedabad, Porbandar, Jodhpur and Sambalpur to achieve and sustain sanitation improvements; improve the management of liquid waste; and achieve a convergence of the various schemes of the national, state and local governments to move towards safely managed sanitation. MISAAL also engages with the USAID-funded national Project Management Unit housed in the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to disseminate learnings from pilots and tools developed by UMC.MISAAL will also use FY 2019 funds to scale up WASH solutions developed in partnership with city managers' associations and urban development departments of the states of Gujarat, Rajasthan and Odisha to other cities. MISAAL also fosters city to city partnerships between Indian and US cities and leverages international learning through the International City/County Management Association (ICMA). For example, UMC is leading a delegation from the partner states and cities to the city of Pearland, Texas followed by participation in the ICMA's Annual Conference 2019 at Nashville, Tennessee in October 2019. The impact of the proposed interventions will be that the cities of Ahmedabad, Porbandar, Jodhpur and Sambalpur will be at the forefront of sustainable sanitation development and will act as models for other large and small cities in their respective states and centre.

The improved forest management planning will reduce forest degradation and improve the quality of the forests, thereby helping to increase carbon sequestration and reduce greenhouse gas emissions while also enhancing other ecosystem services such as water flows and biodiversity. This is a bold paradigm shift for the GOI, moving from a selective and vertical primary care approach to integrated service delivery at the primary care level. ..With FY 2022 funds, the NISHTHA project will support the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM -ABHIM) initiative through integrated TB, maternal and child health, and family planning activities. NISHTHA will provide technical assistance to strengthen the GOI's capacity to deliver comprehensive primary health care services to vulnerable populations. Interventions will ensure continuum of care vertically and a network of care approaches that include linkages to GOI insurance and social support schemes and will strengthen the quality of services delivered through Health and Wellness centers. The activity will address some of the systemic challenges and bottlenecks in terms of human resources career progression pathways, supply chain management, and community engagement by establishing institutional structures to strengthen Comprehensive Primary Health Care. USAID will provide support to fill service delivery gaps in reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health care and TB to reduce out of pocket expenditures and improve access to services for the most vulnerable populations in urban and rural India. Support will strengthen timely detection and treatment of TB patients much closer to their places of residence, thus decreasing loss to follow up and improving treatment completion. The activity will promote well-being across communities to decrease morbidity and ultimately reduce disease burden, while mitigating the impact of the COVID-19... ..Adaptation-Indirect key issue attributed funds will provide TA for operationalizing greener and climate resilient health facilities in all NISHTHA supported states....

description.narrative: (India): ..This mechanism is a key component of USAID's Global.Accelerator to End Tuberculosis. There has been a strong commitment for a.TB-free India from the highest levels of the Government of India, which has an.ambitious National Strategic Plan (NSP) to eliminate TB by 2025. The burden of.undetected TB is high in many settings, especially in high-risk groups which.are identified under the country's new National Strategic Plan (2017-25)..Mapping of high-risk groups and carefully planned systematic screening for active.disease among them has improved early case detection that may help to reduce.the risks of TB transmission, poor treatment outcomes, undesirable health.consequences, and adverse social and economic effects of the disease. title.narrative: Skill Development in Fecal Sludge and Septage Management (FSSM)

description.narrative: (India): Using FY 2020 funds, USAID/India will continue support for the Skill Development in Fecal Sludge and Septage Management Sector in Indian Towns and Cities (SDFSSM) activity which commenced in 2019. The goal of the activity is to build the capacity of municipal officials, private sector players, NGOs and students in fecal sludge and septage management (FSSM) to improve Indians' access to safely managed sanitation services with a focus on municipalities in the Ganges River Basin. The activity will also contribute to the development of a sanitation ecosystem which will strengthen private sector interest and investment which is fundamentally important for the development of the Indian sanitation sector. ..More specifically, the activity implementing partner will conduct several different training courses on the operation and maintenance of fecal sludge treatment plants (FSTP), sewage treatment plants (STP) and sewer lines. Courses will include a two-day safety training session for sanitation workers and plant operators, a one week course on the design and operation of fecal sludge treatment units; a three-month certificate course on the operation and maintenance of FSTPs and STPs; a one-year course on off site treatment methods including septic tanks, anaerobic reactors, planted gravel filters etc.; and a one-year course on urban water management including wastewater recycling and water conservation..

title.narrative: Closing the Gaps in TB Care Cascade

description.narrative: (India): ..The goal of the project is to strengthen district health systems to reduce gaps in diagnosis, treatment, and recurrence-free survival of drug-sensitive (DS-TB) and drug resistant (DR-TB) TB, in order to achieve high quality and equitable care. .. ..With FY 2022 funds, this activity will employ a variety of approaches that are needed on the spectrum of TB care. This includes identifying "missing" cases by addressing gaps in delayed care-seeking pathways, inadequate access to TB diagnostics for drug-susceptibility testing-guided treatment, and active case-finding. It will also address barriers to treatment access with decentralized access to treatment, tracking patient mobility and migration, and improved provider-patient interactions. A focus will also be on improving treatment outcomes and recurrence-free survival with improved TB counseling, enhanced care models for co-morbidities, and adherence monitoring. The activity will work on improving programmatic management of latent TB infections by targeting and monitoring high-risk groups for testing and TB preventive therapy with care cascade. Finally, interventions will be taken to health systems by developing the capacity of district leadership, health workers, and the Nikshay digital monitoring and treatment platform infrastructure to coordinate the patient care cascade and improve program performance. .. ..This intervention supports the U.S. Government's Global Tuberculosis Strategy which aims to reach every person with TB, cure those in need of treatment, and prevent the spread of disease and new infections. .

Narmada Landscape Restoration Project (NLRP) in Khargone district of Madhya Pradesh is being supported by United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and NTPC Ltd. NLRP will demonstrate the interdependency of upstream sustainable forest and farm practices on downstream water resources. Through demonstration in Barwaha block, Khargone district, the project aims to establish an incentivization mechanism that can continue to support the forest and farm communities around Narmada to maintain sustainable landscape practices that will positively impact the water quality and quantity in Narmada tributaries. The project activities are linked to supply of water to Indore Municipality from Jalud and therefore requires strong working relationship with Indore Municipal Corporation (IMC) and Government of Madhya Pradesh. NLRP activities will be implemented in two distinct zones, one dominated by forest and the other by agriculture landscape, and field-level execution will be carried out with support from selected local organizations.

description.narrative: (India): . .India contributes 20 percent of the world's child deaths, 10 percent of maternal deaths, and is the largest contributor to prematurity-related complications. This activity will contribute to the UN Sustainable Development Goals and is aligned with the Global Strategy of Ending Preventable Maternal Mortality. The program will enhance the capacity of the Government of India (GOI), private sector, and civil society to work together to improve health outcomes. .With FY 2022 funding, SAKSHAM will work closely with national and state governments to provide targeted technical assistance to state health societies, while also demonstrating innovative models at the district level. The project will focus on building sustainable state-level capabilities for high impact maternal, newborn, and child health service provision through improved quality of care and innovations, and will ensure that these interventions are adapted and scaled by the government and sustained through national and state budget and human resource provisions. .With FY 2022 funds, activities will focus on: 1) using Living Labs and Human Centered Design approaches to set up hybrid learning models; 2) leveraging the Mobile Medical Unit model in the Assam tea gardens; 3) applying data analytics to optimize data platforms, dashboards, and supply chain software for evidence-based decision-making, 4) engaging the private sector, including local entrepreneurs, businesses, and private healthcare providers in rural/tribal areas; 5) harnessing innovations through an Impact Lab to advance promising technologies; and 6) implementing Behavior Change Communication using innovative strategies for demand generation for quality MNCH services.

title.narrative: Centre for MicroFinance (CMF)- Nurturing Early Literacy Project

description.narrative: (India): .The Nurturing Early Literacy project implemented by the Centre for Micro-Finance will continue to implement activities that build a strong foundation of early literacy competencies for 93,000 students across the states of Rajasthan, Maharashtra, and Karnataka. This activity closely aligns with Goal 1 of the USAID Education Strategy. As per the latest Annual Status of Education Report (ASER), over half of fifth graders in rural India are unable to read at the second grade level in their regional language. To address this, the project, through its four sub-partners, will continue to support community, school, and e- libraries in all three states; develop training modules and conduct training programs for teachers to create a classroom environment that is conducive to learning so that there is a shift from the prevalent rote-based pedagogy in India to one in which the child is an active learner who can effectively learn sounds and symbols, read and write with comprehension, and apply their knowledge in everyday life. .

title.narrative: Scaling-up Early Learning - Room to Read India Trust (RTR)

description.narrative: (India): .Using FY 2018 funds, USAID/India will continue to support the ongoing Room to Read activity that is improving the educational outcomes of primary school children in the states of Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh; this activity has come out as the best performing model among all education activities supported by USAID India as evaluated recently through a USAID Washington supported external assessment. The activity will work closely with government counterparts to build the capacity of education functionaries and provide policy inputs, enabling state governments to implement more effective education interventions. This will play a very important role in India's journey to self-reliance in education because it includes institutional strengthening as a key focus. Further, an educated Indian population will drive inclusive and sustainable development, open new markets and support U.S. prosperity and security objectives, which is the second Strategic Objective of the Joint Strategic Plan. In addition to capacity building of government staff, the activity will continue to train teachers in reading instruction and instill reading habits in students with the effective use of school libraries. The activity will also provide libraries with hundreds of additional books of levels appropriate for early graders. The implementing partner will ensure that all teaching and learning materials developed under the activity will align with state government curriculums. Finally, the activity will support research in multilingual education for the benefit of tribal areas in project states, as well as undertake cost analyses on the transition from pilot project to a scaled up project. With FY 2018 funds, the project will reach at least 250,000 students directly and about four million indirectly. .

The Industry Advisory Council established under the RISE initiative will extend its footprint to the region by facilitating U.S. and Indian entities to engage with policy makers in India and other South Asian countries to capitalize on market opportunities.
